assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology led to GLP-1 receptor agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits shown in large outcome trials. Mechanistic originality, clinical scale and durability of impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst established GLP-1 secretion and physiology in humans, Drucker clarified its biology and the role of GLP-2 and the receptor pathway, and Mojsov contributed to the identification of the bioactive peptide form. Knudsen's medicinal-chemistry work on long-acting analogues is major but industrial, and the list may omit other early contributors such as Joel Habener; allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed over two decades of independent clinical use and outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the therapeutic reach.
uncertainties: Priority dispute around the isolation and sequencing of the active GLP-1 peptide (I rely on memory and have not verified details).
Whether a physiology-plus-drug-development compound discovery can be fairly split into three laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision and has become a standard tool across the field; it is original, widely adopted and clearly Nobel-scale as a methodological invention.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and the demonstration of neuronal control (Boyden, Deisseroth, also Miesenböck's earlier genetic approach) are distinct steps; six credited names exceed three places, so any trio leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Extensively reproduced for roughly two decades; clinical translation (retinal optogenetic vision restoration) is early but the basic-science impact is mature.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited people is contested and a three-person limit is hard to justify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib proved that inhibiting a defined oncogenic kinase can convert a fatal leukemia into a chronic manageable disease, establishing the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy. Impact on patients and the field is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the compound discovery programme, Druker drove the clinical translation, and Sawyers was key to understanding resistance and second-generation inhibitors. This forms a coherent trio, although the original BCR-ABL oncogene biology (Rowley, Baltimore and others) lies outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of follow-up and independent confirmation; the paradigm has been replicated in many cancers, so it is mature and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: The prior discoveries of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL are not credited here.
Industrial credit within Novartis may be diffusely allocated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living drugs; the concept and clinical proof are original and consequential.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain built and clinically validated CAR designs with costimulatory domains; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Early CAR conceptual work (Eshhar, Kuwana and others) is not in the supplied credit, so the trio is defensible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up; solid tumours, toxicity and durability remain open, but the haematological success is firmly established.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier cancer-immunology prize (checkpoint blockade) may affect timing.
Attribution among early CAR pioneers is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating TNF as a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis changed the treatment of chronic inflammatory disease and led to a drug class used worldwide; it is a clean bench-to-bedside story with a clear mechanistic insight.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly identified TNF's dominant role in synovial cytokine networks and led the first clinical trials, a natural two-person allocation; contributions of those who cloned TNF or developed the antibodies lie outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and expansion to Crohn's disease, psoriasis and others; recognition is mature.
uncertainties: The role of the original TNF discoverers and antibody engineers may weigh in a committee discussion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and have markedly reduced cervical precancer incidence, with emerging evidence of cancer reduction; it is a major preventive-medicine achievement that builds on the earlier link of HPV to cervical cancer.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs, and Frazer's group contributed in parallel with Zhou's work on VLP expression; other contributors such as Jian Zhou (deceased) are not in the supplied credit, so a fair configuration is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data are now substantial; the cancer endpoint evidence is increasing, so timing is good.
uncertainties: Prior HPV-cancer link already recognised in 2008.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense therapy for SMA (nusinersen) turned a lethal infant neurodegenerative disease into a treatable one, and validated antisense oligonucleotides as a modality. The mechanistic insight is original and the clinical effect dramatic.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the SMN2 exon 7 splicing mechanisms and the ASO target, while Bennett's chemistry and development programme brought it to the clinic; the pairing is natural, though other academic contributors (for example Hua and Krainer co-workers) and Ionis team members are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with long-term follow-up and independent confirmation, but the modality is still young and its long-term durability is under study.
uncertainties: Maturity of the antisense field as a whole.
Whether Nobel recognition is better reserved for the modality rather than a single drug.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explained how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, connecting infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence; it is a conceptually clear discovery with wide biological significance.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger 2'3'-cGAMP, and Barber identified STING; other credited names (Ishikawa, Wu, Sun) contributed as co-discoverers or trainees, so the core attribution is fairly clear.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in basic research, but clinical translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) is still incomplete, so the prize may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is not yet established.
Credit for STING discovery involved several laboratories.
